2916.text:
Start date: February 2027 · Duration: 6 months
Please include your latest academic transcripts with your application. Applications submitted without transcripts will not be considered.
In this 6-month internship or master thesis starting in February 2027, you will build a multi-agent RFP assistant leveraging agentic workflows. In the context of offer management, AI can support the offer team in preparing proposals.
You will adapt an agentic AI framework, originally designed for agile software delivery, to RFP (Request for Proposal) response management. You will design and prototype a custom module mapping product development phases to the bid lifecycle, with specialized AI agents covering requirements extraction, gap analysis, solution design, work breakdown, effort estimation and compliance checking.
Your tasks
Deliver a working proof-of-concept of an RFP assistant: a structured, repeatable workflow where RFP requirements are analyzed, assumptions are registered, a solution is designed with traceable justification, and a costed work breakdown is produced
Work on real procurement contexts and produce reusable artifacts, configurations and templates applicable across multiple bids
Validate the approach on realistic RFP cases, measuring the reduction in effort and the improvement in proposal quality
Write an article, to be published on the web, presenting the results of your work
What we offer
A dynamic, collaborative workplace with a highly motivated, multicultural team working across international sites
The chance to make a difference in people's lives by building innovative solutions
Internal coding events such as Hackathons and Brownbag sessions, plus our technical blog
Monthly After-Works organized at each location
About your profile
Knowledge of NLP and of techniques for training, tuning and deploying machine learning models; knowledge of deep learning development
Practical software development skills in one or more programming languages (e.g. Python, Java)
Nice to have: knowledge of commonly used Azure or AWS services and of foundation models

2918.text:
Start date: February 2027 · Duration: 6 months
Please include your latest academic transcripts with your application. Applications submitted without transcripts will not be considered.
In this 6-month internship starting in February 2027, you will explore real-time data processing at scale with Apache Kafka, Apache Flink and Apache Spark, and help us define guidelines for choosing the right framework.
Your tasks
Understand the fundamental concepts of Kafka, Flink and Spark, including their architecture and use cases
Implement a pipeline processing streaming data from a single source using Kafka and Flink/Spark, going as far as possible with insights and optimizations
Build a second, more complex pipeline: Database → Debezium → Kafka → Flink/Spark → transactional and analytical queries
Handle multiple tables and implement watermarking to ensure synchronized data processing
Compare Flink and Spark on performance, ease of use and suitability for specific use cases
Document your findings and propose guidelines for choosing between the two frameworks

About your profile
Bachelor's or Master's student in Computer Science, Data Engineering or a related field
Interest in distributed systems and real-time data processing
Programming skills (e.g. Java, Scala or Python) and knowledge of SQL
Curiosity, autonomy and good analytical skills

2995.text:
Start date: Spring 2027 · Duration: 6 months
Please include your latest academic transcripts with your application. Applications submitted without transcripts will not be considered.
You will be connected to a real ELCA product initiative with direct business impact . Many customers hold millions of documents in legacy systems, file shares and older document management platforms, and migrating this content into a modern platform is often slow and expensive. You will work with realistic customer data, collaborate closely with ELCA product experts and architects, and, as soon as the solution reaches a testable stage, it will be evaluated on real migration scenarios.
You will join the Mosaic product team (ELCA's document and information management suite, including Mosaic eanna, operated as SaaS on the ELCA multi-tenant hosting platform) and design an AI-powered migration pipeline , in which LLMs classify documents and extract their metadata based on prompts instead of costly custom migration projects.
You will join the AI Innovation team and design the AI-assisted diagnostic and AI recommendation engine.
Your tasks
Design and implement a lightweight migration client with a minimal installation footprint (e.g. embedded file-based database), including a first standard crawler connected to the existing document import REST API
Extend the document import processing with an LLM-based classification step that assigns document types and extracts metadata based on the target system's taxonomy
Build a human-in-the-loop feedback cycle in which prompts and indexing rules can be refined between migration rounds, with AI-classified documents flagged for review
Evaluate the approach end-to-end on a realistic dataset (accuracy per document type, confidence levels, unclassified documents) and give recommendations for productive use
Apply ELCA's patterns for multi-tenancy, security and data protection, with support from ELCA architects
Depending on progress: develop a configuration screen for prompts and a monitoring view to follow classification quality
What we offer
A dynamic, collaborative workplace with a highly motivated, multicultural team working across international sites
The chance to make a difference in people's lives by building innovative solutions
Close mentoring by experienced architects and product experts, and a clear path from prototype to product
Internal coding events such as Hackathons and Brownbag sessions, plus our technical blog
Monthly After-Works organized at each location
About your profile
Strong computer science fundamentals (ETH or equivalent Master's degree) and a keen interest in generative AI (LLMs, document classification, information extraction)
Solid programming skills in Java ; experience with Spring Boot is a strong plus, Angular is a plus
Good understanding of REST APIs and data integration; knowledge of Docker / Kubernetes is a plus
Ability to design an end-to-end solution, from prototype to evaluation; autonomous and results-driven
Analytical and curious, with good communication skills and team spirit
Professional working proficiency in English and German ; French is a plus

2996.text:
Start date: Spring 2027 · Duration: 6 months
Please include your latest academic transcripts with your application. Applications submitted without transcripts will not be considered.
You will be connected to a real ELCA product initiative with direct impact on how the product evolves. Mosaic eDossier, ELCA's configurable document and dossier management solution, is used daily by many end users at banks, public administrations and companies. It offers a large number of features built over many years, but today we have little visibility into which features are actually used and how . You will collaborate closely with the eDossier product team and architects, and, as soon as the solution reaches a testable stage, it will be evaluated on ELCA-hosted and internal environments.
You will join the Mosaic product team and design a privacy-by-design observability solution that collects backend and UI usage data inside the customer environment, without any external connection, turns it into anonymized statistics, and helps us decide where to improve the product.
Your tasks
Analyze the eDossier architecture (Java/Spring Boot, Angular) and evaluate suitable observability approaches and tools (e.g. OpenTelemetry, Micrometer, Prometheus, Grafana)
Design and implement the collection of backend usage metrics (endpoints called, frequency, user type or tenant, response times)
Design and implement lightweight collection of UI interactions (navigation paths, click sequences, time spent on screens) with minimal performance impact
Build privacy in from the start : anonymization or pseudonymization of users, no document content or personal data, configurable opt-in/opt-out per customer, and an aggregated statistics report that customers can review before export
Create dashboards for the product team and analyze the data to identify unused features, friction points and frequently repeated workflows
Apply AI/machine learning techniques to the usage data , e.g. clustering navigation paths to detect typical workflows, identifying anomalies and unusual usage patterns, or using LLMs to turn statistics into readable insights for the product team
Present concrete, prioritized recommendations to improve the product and document the solution for productive use
Depending on the progress : extend the UI collection to finer-grained interactions such as mouse movements, consolidate reports from several customer environments into a central analysis at ELCA, and prototype simplifications or automations for the most frequently repeated workflows
What we offer
A dynamic, collaborative workplace with a highly motivated, multicultural team working across international sites
The chance to make a difference in people's lives by building innovative solutions
Close mentoring by experienced architects and product experts, and direct influence on the product roadmap
Internal coding events such as Hackathons and Brownbag sessions, plus our technical blog
Monthly After-Works organized at each location
About your profile
Strong computer science fundamentals (ETH or equivalent Master's degree) and a keen interest in AI, Machine learning, observability, data analysis and user experience
Solid programming skills in Java (Spring Boot); knowledge of Angular/TypeScript is a plus
Interest in observability and monitoring tools (e.g. OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, ELK)
First experience in analyzing data and drawing conclusions from it (e.g. Python, SQL, statistics)
Analytical and curious, with good communication skills, team spirit and an interest in product management
Professional working proficiency in English and German ; French is a plus
